intuition.title: Parameters affecting assembly
intuition.summary: The authors identify nanocrystal size/shape uniformity, ligand coating, interparticle spacing, temperature and concentration as assembly variables. Increased concentration and additional heating support aggregation, while longer time is proposed to permit more ordered arrangements. These qualitative relationships are not a fitted optimization model.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; interpretation and cited context are distinguished in the text.

general_background.title: Tributylphosphine as a chalcogen carrier
general_background.summary: Tributylphosphine can react with elemental chalcogen to form a soluble molecular phosphine chalcogenide feed. When that feed supplies growing nanocrystals, its conversion rate affects the availability of chalcogen for nucleation and growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Molecular Control of the Nanoscale: Effect of Phosphine–Chalcogenide Reactivity on CdS–CdSe Nanocrystal Composition and Morphology

general_background.title: TOPO as a coordinating medium
general_background.summary: Trioctylphosphine oxide supplies a coordinating medium in which metal chalcogenide nanocrystals can nucleate and grow. Coordination at the particle surface influences which growth sites remain accessible and how the particles disperse afterward.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Synthesis and characterization of nearly monodisperse CdE (E = sulfur, selenium, tellurium) semiconductor nanocrystallites

general_background.title: Excluding air during colloidal growth
general_background.summary: An argon atmosphere can limit contact between air and reactive precursors during hot colloidal growth. Protecting the feed from oxidation helps keep the supply of growth species distinct from side reactions with air.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Synthesis and characterization of nearly monodisperse CdE (E = sulfur, selenium, tellurium) semiconductor nanocrystallites

general_background.title: Nucleation and size focusing
general_background.summary: A rapid change in precursor availability can create a short nucleation period followed by growth on existing particles. Growth can narrow the size distribution while material is supplied, whereas later ripening can consume smaller particles and change that distribution again.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
